title: How Evals and Prompts Shape Agent Behavior — Preetika Bhateja & Daniel Bump, YouTube Ads
talk_summary: The speakers argue that agent reliability comes from strong LLM-friendly tools, an independent critique/remediation loop, and evals that start small and intuition-driven before scaling to rubrics and LLM judges. They emphasize trace inspection, negative cases, human/LLM agreement monitoring, pattern-level regression analysis, and refreshing test sets with production data.

takeaways.what_they_do: They inspect full agent traces and reasoning, not just pass/fail rates, to find why edge cases fail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you want to know what it's doing look at it at its thinking

takeaways.what_they_do: They start with a few core tasks and explicitly test cases where the agent should not do something bad.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's important to also test the negatives

takeaways.what_they_do: They give raters a clear rubric and concrete examples so pass/fail judgments are consistent and measurable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: providing them with a clear rubric of what they were actually rating with very clear examples

takeaways.what_they_do: They monitor a sample pipeline comparing human/expert ratings against LLM-judge ratings to see whether agreement is in the expected range.
takeaways.evidence_quote: monitoring how a human raider or some expert would rate an eval versus how an LLM would rate it

takeaways.what_they_do: They avoid overfitting to one non-deterministic run and instead measure how often a failure pattern appears across the golden set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: focus on patterns rather than isolated runs

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep test sets representative by refreshing them with production data and investing in online evals.
